verdicts.reason: A keeps the original's centred stack and clear headline > subhead > CTA order. Its flaws are small: the headline is pushed high, leaving a top margin smaller than the bottom one, and the subhead wraps awkwardly, leaving 'four flavours.' alone on its second line. B blows the headline up so far that the subhead and CTA get squeezed into a cramped bottom row. That row has centre-aligned three-line copy sitting next to a button with no shared edge or axis, it sits close to the bottom edge, and it breaks the original's centred top-to-bottom reading order.
